fixes.explanation: No cave in this story. The armor-bearer “…fell on his own sword and died.” (1 Chronicles 10:5) And the next day the Philistines find Saul and his sons fallen on Mount Gilboa. (1 Chronicles 10:8) The text never mentions anyone hiding a body.

That's what they do. The Israelites in the valley saw the army had fled and that Saul and his sons were dead, so they “…abandoned their cities and ran away.” (1 Chronicles 10:7) I think that's a scary moment, friend. The king is gone and the army has fled.

Nothing in the verse mentions sending for help. What it says is that they “…abandoned their cities and ran away.” (1 Chronicles 10:7) Then the Philistines came and occupied their cities. It's a heavy one, friend.

Burning is a natural guess, but the verse doesn't mention fire. It says the Philistines “…came and occupied their cities.” (1 Chronicles 10:7) The Israelites had run away, and the Philistines took over the cities. Occupied is the word the text uses.

Close in spirit, but the verse doesn't mention any tearing down. It says the Philistines “…came and occupied their cities.” (1 Chronicles 10:7) The Israelites had run away, and the Philistines came in. Occupied is the word the text gives us.

They did the opposite, friend. The Philistines “…sent messengers throughout the land of the Philistines to proclaim the news in the temple of their idols and among their people.” (1 Chronicles 10:9) They wanted it known everywhere. The news went to the temple of their idols and to the people.

Yes. All their men of valor “…set out and retrieved the bodies of Saul and his sons and brought them to Jabesh.” (1 Chronicles 10:12) They heard what had been done, and they went and got the bodies. I think that's a brave and kind thing to do, friend.

The text doesn't send them to fight at the temple. It says their men of valor “…set out and retrieved the bodies of Saul and his sons and brought them to Jabesh.” (1 Chronicles 10:12) Their job was getting the bodies home.

No gifts are mentioned. Their men of valor “…set out and retrieved the bodies of Saul and his sons and brought them to Jabesh.” (1 Chronicles 10:12) The text says they went themselves, and it says nothing of buying anything.

Celebrating isn't what the text says. They “…buried their bones under the oak in Jabesh and fasted seven days.” (1 Chronicles 10:12) Fasting means going without food, and that's the opposite of a feast. I think this was a time of mourning, friend.

Marching isn't in the text. They “…buried their bones under the oak in Jabesh and fasted seven days.” (1 Chronicles 10:12) Nobody is said to march anywhere. Fasting means going without food for those seven days.

Yes. The writer says Saul “…even consulted a medium for guidance…” (1 Chronicles 10:13) That's one of the reasons given for his unfaithfulness. A medium is someone who claims to speak with the dead. The next verse goes on to say he failed to inquire of the LORD. (1 Chronicles 10:14)

The text says it did happen. Saul “…even consulted a medium for guidance…” (1 Chronicles 10:13) A medium is someone who claims to speak with the dead. That's part of the reason Chronicles gives for his death. The next verse goes on to say he failed to inquire of the LORD. (1 Chronicles 10:14)
Yes. The LORD “…turned the kingdom over to David son of Jesse.” (1 Chronicles 10:14) The writer says it goes to David, friend. Saul's story closes, and David's is coming.
